questions.prompt: SKIP LOCKED returns no row while an available item is locked elsewhere. What can the service conclude?

options.label: No matching row was acquired by that statement; it cannot infer sold out.
Every unit has been sold permanently.
The database proves strict first-come-first-served admission.

questions.explanation: The statement skips locked rows and does not expose a complete availability view. Neither permanent inventory exhaustion nor waiting-room fairness follows from an empty result.

questions.prompt: A waiting room limits accounts to one signed admission token each. What remains unresolved?

options.label: Eligibility and abuse policy; one account does not prove one legitimate human.
Cryptographic signatures guarantee that every account belongs to a different human.
Inventory ownership is automatically correct without a transaction.

questions.explanation: A signature protects a token’s integrity under its design, not the uniqueness of a person. Identity policy still matters, and inventory needs its own atomic transition.

questions.prompt: B’s hold expired; A now owns the unit. B’s external payment succeeds late. What should completion do?

options.label: Reject the stale inventory transition and record/reconcile B’s payment outcome.
Sell A’s held unit to B because payment delivery arrived last.
Ignore the external result because a zero-row update refunded it automatically.

questions.explanation: The current hold/version guards protect A’s ownership. They do not undo an external charge. Reconciliation or compensation follows the provider and product contract; last-write-wins is unsafe.

questions.prompt: The chosen rule permits completion only while expires_at is strictly greater than now. At the exact expiry tick, what applies?

options.label: Completion is ineligible; expiry may win the guarded transition.
Both completion and expiry must commit independently.
Completion always wins regardless of the database’s current hold version.

questions.explanation: Under this explicit boundary, equality fails the completion predicate and satisfies expiry’s time predicate. State, identity and version still determine whether an update can commit. Both transitions cannot independently own the same unit.
